paragraphs: Luton Borough Council runs its own fostering service, and the independent agencies shown above also approve carers in the town. Fostering for the council means caring for Luton's own children, with the council's social workers supporting you; an independent agency carries out your assessment, approves and supervises you itself, and looks after children placed with it by councils.

In March 2025 the council said it looks after more than 300 children and young people, and that many of them live outside Luton because there are not enough fostering families in the town. Its sufficiency strategy for 2025 to 2030 puts recruiting and keeping its own carers first. It records that 26.2% of placements in March 2025 were more than 20 miles away and aims to bring that under 18% within three years, and it plans to recruit 24 new council fostering households between April 2025 and March 2027. It also wants to reduce its use of agency placements and wants its carers to reflect Luton's cultural, ethnic and faith diversity, working with churches, mosques, temples and cultural groups to reach more people.

The council pays a weekly allowance for each child, from £189 for babies to £288 for 16 and 17-year-olds, and a weekly skills fee per child that rises with experience, from £145.90 in a carer's first year with Luton to £259.13 after five years. Birthday, festive and holiday allowances are paid on top, along with a £1,000 contribution towards Council Tax. Our Luton allowance page has the full scale.

Luton recruits with Central Bedfordshire and Bedford Borough as Foster East – Luton and Bedfordshire. With government backing, the three councils are building a shared fostering hub that aims to raise foster capacity across their areas to 478 places by 2028/29, part of a national aim of 10,000 more foster places by April 2029.

Each of Luton's own carers has a supervising social worker and joins the Luton Foster Carers Association on approval. Carers complete at least six training activities in their first year and three a year after that, and there is a yearly celebration event. Since August 2025 the council has run a Mockingbird group, in which an experienced hub home carer supports a cluster of fostering families; the first has nine carers and ten children. To start, call Foster East on 01582 547 633 (the council lists 8am to 8pm, Monday to Sunday) and speak to two or three of the agencies above. The Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire and Milton Keynes pages list more services nearby.
